articles.summary: India continued its medal charge at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026, adding seven medals on September 27 before Esha Singh opened India's medal account
articles.body: India continued its medal charge at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026, adding seven medals on September 27 before Esha Singh opened India's medal account on September 28 with a silver in the women's 25m pistol. The latest additions have taken India's overall tally to 39 medals: 4 gold, 17 silver and 18 bronze. India entered September 28 with 37 medals after a seven-medal haul on September 27.Esha Singh added the latest silver medal to India’s tally after finishing second in the women’s 25m pistol final. She was locked on 38 points with China’s Xiao Jiaruixian, with the Chinese shooter eventually prevailing in the deciding shoot-off. Pincky Balhara then added a bronze in the women’s -78kg Kurash event after losing her semifinal against South Korea’s Mo Sumin.India had enjoyed a particularly productive September 27, winning seven medals, four silver and three bronze. Ancy Sojan Edappilly and Sarvesh Kushare won silver in women's long jump and men's high jump respectively, while squash stars Abhay Singh and Anahat Singh also finished runners-up. Parul Chaudhary, Tejaswin Shankar and Harita Bhadra added bronze medals in athletics.India's Latest Asian Games 2026 MedalsSilver - Esha Singh: Esha added India's 38th medal of the Games with silver articles.title: At 19, Pincky Balhara lost three family members ahead of Asian Games debut; Now, she is only Indian to win multiple Kurash medals
articles.summary: Three family deaths in quick succession could have brought Pincky Balhara’s sporting journey to a halt.
articles.body: Three family deaths in quick succession could have brought Pincky Balhara’s sporting journey to a halt. Instead, the Delhi athlete carried her grief into the competition arena, turned her father’s dream into motivation and went on to win an Asian Games medal.Eight years after her historic silver at the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games, Balhara returned to the continental podium on Monday, winning bronze in the women’s -78kg Kurash event at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Games. The bronze is Balhara’s second Asian Games medal in Kurash, following her silver in the women’s -52kg category in Jakarta. She has now become the only Indian athlete to win multiple Asian Games medals in Kurash.What is Kurash?Kurash is a traditional Central Asian martial art that originated in the region and is particularly associated with Uzbekistan. It made its Asian Games debut at the 2018 Jakarta Games. The basic objective is simple: throw the opponent onto their back while remaining in a standing position. Unlike judo or Brazilian jiu-jitsu, Kurash does not involve prolonged ground fighting.From judo mats to KurashBorn on October 20, 1998, in Neb Sarai, Delhi, Balhara began training in judo when she was nine. Her maternal uncle, Samundar Tokas, a former judoka and coach, played a major role in her early development.She quickly established herself in judo, winning gold at the 2018 Asian Junior Judo Championships. But she missed out on India's judo squad for the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games. That disappointment opened another door.With Kurash making its Asian Games debut in Jakarta, Balhara entered the trials. The sport, which shares similarities with judo but is contested entirely from a standing position, offered her another route to the continental stage. She made the team and was soon heading to Jakarta.Three deaths changed everythingBut just weeks before the Games, Balhara's life was shattered. She lost her cousin brother first, followed by her father, who died of a heart attack, and then her grandfather. The three deaths came in quick succession, leaving the teenager struggling to cope with the loss.Her father had been particularly excited about her selection for the Asian Games. After his death, Balhara initially did not want to compete. Her uncle, however, pushed her to continue, reminding her of her father's hopes for her career.She returned to training while dealing with grief and also had to make the weight for her 52kg category. She later recalled going to the gym at night because she feared people would judge her for returning to training so soon after her father's death.Balhara eventually made it to the 2018 Asian Games and produced a remarkable run. At just 19, she reached the women's -52kg Kurash final, becoming one of India's first Asian Games medallists in the sport. She eventually lost to Uzbekistan's Gulnor Sulaymanova and settled for silver.Balhara later recalled her father's prediction before the Games: that she would win silver rather than gold. When she finished second, she remembered his words. At Aichi-Nagoya, Balhara began her campaign with a 3-0 quarterfinal victory over South Korea's Garam Lim, securing her place in the semifinals and guaranteeing India another Kurash medal.She then faced South Korea's Sumin Mo in the last four. Mo won 5-0, sending Balhara into the bronze-medal position.Eight years after her first Asian Games medal, Balhara was back on the podium.Pincky Balhara's Asian Games recordYearGamesCategoryResult2018JakartaWomen's -52kg🥈 Silver2022HangzhouWomen's KurashQuarterfinal2026Aichi-NagoyaWomen's -78kg🥉 BronzeStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vithya Ramraj wins bronze in 400m hurdles, adds second medal at Asian Games
articles.summary: Vithya Ramraj added a bronze medal to her Asian Games 2026 tally after finishing third in the women’s 400m hurdles final in Nagoya on Monday.
articles.body: Vithya Ramraj added a bronze medal to her Asian Games 2026 tally after finishing third in the women’s 400m hurdles final in Nagoya on Monday.Ramraj clocked a personal best of 54.75 seconds to finish behind Mariam Kareem of the UAE, who won gold in 54.31, and Kazakhstan’s Adelina Zems, who took silver in 54.58.The 26-year-old was part of India’s silver-medal winning mixed 4x400m relay team earlier in the Games, running the anchor leg and producing a strong finish to help India hold on to second place. The Indian quartet of T S Manu, Poovamma Raju, Vithya and T Vishal clocked 3:14.46.Asian Games Full Coverage|Medal Tally|ScheduleHer compatriot Anu Raghavan finished fifth in 55.88 seconds, also recording a personal best.The medal also adds to Ramraj's Asian Games record. She had won bronze in the women's 400m hurdles at the 2023 Hangzhou Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cuatro muertos y 12 desaparecidos en una montaña de Nepal por una avalancha
articles.standfirst: Todas las víctimas mortales y los desaparecidos son ciudadanos nepalíes que se encontraban en el campamento base preparándose para la llegada de clientes extranjeros
articles.summary: Todas las víctimas mortales y los desaparecidos son ciudadanos nepalíes que se encontraban en el campamento base preparándose para la llegada de clientes extranjeros
articles.body: Equipos de rescate buscaban el lunes a una docena de personas arrastradas por una avalancha que mató al menos a cuatro individuos en una montaña nepalí durante condiciones meteorológicas adversas. Los rescatistas de la Asociación Nacional de Guías de Montaña de Nepal, que lidera las operaciones, informaron que recuperaron dos cuerpos más el lunes, sumándose a los dos hallados el domingo. Hay doce personas desaparecidas. Ocho experimentados guías de montaña de la asociación aprovecharon la mejora del tiempo para excavar en la nieve que había cubierto las tiendas de campaña en el campamento base. Diez personas fueron rescatadas del monte Himlung, una cima de 7.126 metros situada en el centro-norte de Nepal, después de que la avalancha golpeara la zona el domingo. Todas las víctimas mortales y los desaparecidos eran ciudadanos nepalíes. Se encontraban en el campamento base preparándose para la llegada de clientes extranjeros que escalarían la cima durante la temporada de otoño —iniciada este mes— cuando fueron arrastrados por el alud. Helicópteros trasladaron los cuerpos al aeropuerto de Katmandú. Familiares y amigos presentes en la morgue del hospital no hicieron declaraciones. Las inundaciones y los deslizamientos de tierra en el distrito de Manang, donde se encuentra la montaña, fueron provocados por fuertes lluvias, según informó la oficina administrativa del distrito. Se habían emitido alertas por condiciones meteorológicas adversas en toda la nación del Himalaya. La agencia de gestión de desastres de Nepal comunicó que otras 21 personas han fallecido y cinco más permanecen desaparecidas en diferentes partes del país entre el jueves y el domingo. Nepal se está recuperando de unas inundaciones devastadoras ocurridas en agosto, que arrasaron varias aldeas y dejaron más de 1.400 muertos y cerca de 6.000 desaparecidos.

articles.title: Asian Games: Gulveer Singh bags second silver with 1500m personal best time in Japan
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian distance runner Gulveer Singh continued his impressive campaign at the Asian Games 2026, winning his second silver medal in Japan with a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian distance runner Gulveer Singh continued his impressive campaign at the Asian Games 2026, winning his second silver medal in Japan with a personal best performance in the men's 1500m final on Monday.Gulveer clocked 3:36.72 to finish second behind Japan's Kazuto Iizawa, who clinched gold, while another Japanese runner, Nagiya Mori, took bronze in 3:37.92. India's other finalist, Yoonus Shah, finished ninth with a time of 3:43.88.The silver added to Gulveer's medal collection at the ongoing Games, having already secured a second-place finish in the men's 10,000m. His latest podium finish also provided a bright spot for Indian athletics on a day when defending champion Avinash Sable missed out on a medal in the 3000m steeplechase.Gulveer's double silver underlined his consistency across two demanding distance events, as he improved his personal best in the 1500m to finish among the leading runners in the field.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleVithya breaks PT Usha's record with 400m hurdles bronzeEarlier, Vithya Ramraj delivered a historic performance in the women's 400m hurdles, winning bronze with a personal best of 54.75 seconds and breaking a national record that had stood for more than four decades.The 28-year-old from Coimbatore finished behind UAE's Mariam Kareem, who won gold in a Games-record 54.31 seconds, and Kazakhstan's Adelina Zems, who took silver in a personal best of 54.58.Vithya bettered the 55.42 seconds recorded by legendary Indian athlete PT Usha at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics. It was her second medal at the Games, following silver in the 4x400m mixed relay.India's Anu Raghavan finished fifth in the final with a personal best of 55.88 seconds.Sable's title defence ends in disappointmentThe day's biggest setback for India came in the men's 3000m steeplechase, where defending champion and Games record holder Avinash Sable finished fourth despite clocking a season-best 8:21.67.The 32-year-old two-time Olympian from Maharashtra, who has been troubled by injuries, finished 4.31 seconds behind Japan's Ryuji Miura, who won gold in a Games-record 8:17.36. Miura's compatriot Ryoma Aoki claimed silver in a personal best of 8:17.60, while Qatar's Zakaria Elahlaami took bronze in 8:18.13.Sable's failure to defend his title was a major disappointment for India, particularly after he had established himself as one of the country's leading distance runners.There was further frustration in the women's discus throw, where Commonwealth Games bronze medallist Seema Kaliramna finished fourth despite recording a personal best of 59.88m in her fifth attempt. All three medal winners crossed the 60m mark.In the men's 400m hurdles, Santosh Kumar Tamilarasan finished seventh in the eight-man final with a timing of 49.95 seconds.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games: Parul Chaudhary wins second bronze in 5000m after steeplechase medal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's Parul Chaudhary added another medal to her Asian Games 2026 tally, clinching bronze in the women's 5000m final with a time of 15:14.61.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's Parul Chaudhary added another medal to her Asian Games 2026 tally, clinching bronze in the women's 5000m final with a time of 15:14.61.Bahrain's Winfred Yavi claimed gold in 15:10.18, while Japan's Nozomi Tanaka took silver with a timing of 15:11.65.The experienced Indian long-distance runner secured her second medal at the ongoing Games after winning bronze in the women's 3000m steeplechase earlier in the competition. Her latest podium finish added to an impressive Asian Games record, having also won gold in the women's 5000m and silver in the steeplechase at the Hangzhou Games in 2022.The 5000m bronze further strengthened India's athletics medal tally, with Parul once again demonstrating her ability to compete in multiple events at the continental level.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleParul adds another medal after steeplechase successParul had earlier produced a record-breaking performance in the women's 3000m steeplechase, winning bronze in 9:08.67 and improving her own national record. She became the first Indian woman to break the 9:10 barrier in the event.The Indian stayed with the leading group through much of the race and was in contention for silver around the halfway mark. However, she could not maintain her position in the closing stages and finished 2.46 seconds behind Kazakhstan's Norah Tanui, who won silver in 9:06.82.Bahrain's Winfred Yavi claimed the gold medal in a Games-record time of 9:04.36, while India's other entrant, Ankita, finished fourth in 9:19.24.The steeplechase bronze was a significant achievement for Parul, who had bounced back from a fourth-place finish in the 1500m to reach the podium. Her latest success in the 5000m further highlighted her versatility and endurance across distance events.A second consecutive Asian Games campaign with medalsParul had enjoyed a successful outing at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2022, winning gold in the women's 5000m and silver in the 3000m steeplechase. She has now added two bronze medals in Japan, including her latest achievement in the 5000m.Her performances across the two editions underline her sustained presence among India's leading distance runners and provide another boost to the country's athletics campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
